lines: An unchanging landscape, shallow noon
Under the overpass, indigo squared, lying there as I am
On a blank-page life, a single clap rings out
Today again I sang of my empty self
So that nothing would change
Inside a notebook where I write a plot with you as the lead
Gas and water cut off; the world and the news are, after all, someone else's affair
Even this life, look, is like ink
The dream I kept drawing in my head back then — the more I grow up
The more it passes its statute of limitations
Even as I just, just look up at the clouds
My vision drifts on today as it always does
In the night I gazed at far away, flowers swim
Enough to be mistaken for spring
As if simply losing sight of you
A life spent looking down so I wouldn't stumble is, somehow,
Made of compromise
I don't believe in the heart, or fate, or love songs, or life
If it won't sell anyway, it's all a waste
Lying sprawled in a present drawn with dreams I spilled on purpose, still as I am
Waiting for the statute of limitations
Just, just the back of my eyelids
Still watching you, drawn far away
In the notebook, in a thin corner of night, flowers swim
In my eyes, once more,
Life is a string of compromises
I knew that long ago
Elma, it's you
You alone are my music
Eighty characters left in this poem
Because a life's worth lies in how it ends
So I just, just keep drawing you alone
The indigo in my vision still blurred as it is
In the sky I gazed at far away, flowers swim
Indigo squared covering these eyes
Just, just
The sky I gazed at far away, you cool off in it
As if simply swimming through the night
